title: Phrasal verbs 6: up/down
subtitle: put up / take down / break down
summary: Learn common phrasal verbs with up and down, from put something up and stand up to break down, let somebody down and turn an offer down.

left.label: up
examples: There was a letter on the floor. I **picked it up** and looked at it.
I can't hear the TV. Can you **turn it up** a bit?

right.label: down
examples: I didn't like the picture, so I **took it down**.
I stopped writing and **put down** my pen.
I **bent down** to tie my shoelace.
The oven is too hot. **Turn it down** to 150 degrees.

lesson.heading: knock down, blow down, cut down
lesson.text: **down** often means that something falls or is brought to the ground: you **knock down** a building, the wind **blows** a tree **down**, you **cut down** a tree. **be knocked down** is what happens to a person hit by a car.

examples.text: Some old houses **were knocked down** to make way for the new shopping centre.
Why did you **cut down** the tree in your garden?
A man **was knocked down** by a car and taken to hospital.
They were able to put out the fire before the house **burnt down**.

lesson.heading: down = getting less
lesson.text: **down** can mean that something becomes less or slower: **slow down** = go more slowly, **calm (somebody) down** = become or make somebody calmer, **cut down (on something)** = do it less often.

examples.text: **Calm down.** There's no point in getting angry.
I'm trying to **cut down on** coffee. I drink too much of it.

lesson.heading: break down and close down
lesson.text: **break down** = stop working (machines, cars, relationships). **close down** or **shut down** = stop doing business.

examples.text: The car **broke down** and I had to phone for help.
Their marriage **broke down** after only a few months.
There used to be a shop at the end of the street. It **closed down** a few years ago.

lesson.heading: let down, turn down, write down
lesson.text: **let somebody down** = disappoint them because you didn't do what they hoped. **turn somebody/something down** = refuse an application or an offer. **write something down** = write it on paper because you may need it later.

examples.text: You can always rely on Paul. He'll never **let you down**.
I applied for several jobs, but I **was turned down** for all of them.
Rachel was offered the job, but she decided to **turn it down**.
I can't remember Ben's address. I **wrote it down**, but I can't find it.

lesson.text: Watch out for *turn down*: it means both 'make quieter or cooler' and 'refuse an offer'.

exercises.prompt: There used to be a tree next to the house, but we ___.
exercises.explanation: cut something down = make a tree fall to the ground.

exercises.prompt: She couldn't hear the radio very well, so she ___.
exercises.explanation: turn something up = make it louder.

exercises.prompt: The music was too loud, so I ___.
exercises.explanation: turn something down = make it quieter.

exercises.prompt: A few trees ___ in the storm last week.
exercises.explanation: blow something down = make it fall to the ground; the trees were blown down by the wind.

exercises.prompt: David was very angry. I tried to ___.
exercises.explanation: calm somebody down = make them less angry or excited.

exercises.prompt: I promised I would help Anna. I don't want to ___.
exercises.explanation: let somebody down = disappoint them by not doing what they hoped.

exercises.prompt: I've forgotten my password. I should have ___.
exercises.explanation: write something down = put it on paper so that you have it later.

exercises.prompt: Sarah applied to study medicine at university, but she ___.
exercises.explanation: turn somebody down = refuse their application.

exercises.statement: There used to be a shop at the end of the street. It closed down a few years ago.
exercises.explanation: Correct. close down (or shut down) = stop doing business.

exercises.prompt: Match each phrasal verb with its meaning.
Does each sentence need up or down?

items.text: I can't hear the TV. Can you turn it ...?
The oven is too hot. Turn it ... to 150 degrees.
I bent ... to tie my shoelace.
I put a picture ... on the wall.
I stopped writing and put ... my pen.
